title: pvIsoVolume
body:
## pvIsoVolume

Keeps the part of the input where a scalar lies between the two bounds of ThresholdRange (inclusive), cutting cells exactly at both iso-values for point arrays; the output is an unstructured grid. Use it for the volume between two levels, e.g. 0.1 < alpha < 0.9 at a phase interface. Unlike threshold, which keeps or drops whole cells, it produces smooth boundaries.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- With a cell array, cells are kept or removed whole instead of being cut.
- ParaView's static range is [0, 0], which keeps almost nothing; always set ThresholdRange.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `IsoVolume`. Identity: `filters/IsoVolume`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Threshold filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). The input needs at least one point- or cell-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
